findings.suggested_fix: After validating the private deadline record and both original container identities/lifecycles, arrange independent best-effort stops for worker and proxy even if ledger lookup or durable fencing fails. Bound ledger-lock acquisition so it cannot indefinitely delay these stops; preserve the ledger and report incomplete fencing without permitting completion/replay. Add tests for a quarantined anchor and unavailable/held ledger lock at expiry, asserting both original containers stop and evidence remains retained.
findings.title: Stop original containers when deadline ledger validation fails
findings.why_it_matters: The external deadline can leave both original containers running indefinitely when the attempt ledger becomes quarantined or unavailable. expire() reads the guarded ledger before entering its cleanup block; a coordinator crash between the database commit and anchor update makes _bound() raise, so the one-shot timer never reaches either kill. The immutable private deadline record already carries the original container identities and lifecycles; containment must remain possible independently of ledger availability, while reporting durable fencing as incomplete.
findings.validation_reason: At reviewed a9c2148, expire() calls _bound at deadline_watchdog.py:223 before either container stop or cleanup finally; a missing/quarantined anchor raises from guarded_store.py:83-93, or the blocking flock at line57 waits indefinitely, so neither original container is stopped; the COMMIT-before-anchor ordering at lines99-101 makes quarantine reachable after coordinator failure, though live incidence was not measured.
